fields.meta_description: What an independent contractor agreement should cover, clause by clause, plus an app that drafts each one from an intake form. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Independent Contractor Agreement Generator
fields.hero_description: Build an app that drafts an independent contractor agreement for each hire, collects the W-9, and files the signed copy.
fields.features_subheading: A template supplies the clauses. The six features below cover the paperwork and records that sit around them.
fields.feature_1:
Agreements drafted from intake answers

Drafts each agreement from what the contractor typed at intake, starting with legal name and entity type. When they work through an LLC, the LLC is named as the party that signs.
fields.feature_2:
Clauses matched to the kind of work

Adds a copyright assignment for creative work and an insurance clause for work on a job site. You decide which clauses each type of work carries, and each new draft picks them up.
fields.feature_3:
Both signatures captured in the app

Collects the contractor's signature and then yours on screen, and saves the signed PDF beside the intake answers. A draft left unsigned for three days triggers a reminder.
fields.feature_4:
A W-9 before the first payment

Asks for a completed W-9 during onboarding and stores it with the agreement. Accounts payable sees a contractor marked ready to pay only once a taxpayer ID is on file for them.
fields.feature_5:
Payment totals for year-end 1099s

Records every paid invoice against the contractor who earned it, in a database you own. In January the yearly total per contractor is ready for whoever prepares your 1099-NEC forms.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to take

Exports the full app to GitHub on paid plans whenever you want it. A developer can add a clause library or a payroll sync there, or you can keep prompting Emergent for the changes.
fields.why_description: Every signed agreement sits next to its W-9 in a database you own, with no cap on how many contractors you add.

fields.usecase_heading: Contractor Agreements by Type of Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Who owns the artwork once the invoice is paid

The copyright in a commissioned illustration stays with the artist unless the contract moves it. A logo fits none of the nine categories of contractor work that can be made for hire. Lumen Studio's agreement adds a written assignment instead: ownership passes on the last payment, and the illustrator keeps portfolio rights.
fields.tab_content_2:
One intake, then the agreement and the W-9

Northwind Agency signs on 40 contractors a quarter through a single intake. Emergent drafts each agreement from the answers and requests a W-9 before any invoice is paid. A ledger totals payments per person and flags anyone whose 2026 payments reach $2,000, the 1099-NEC reporting line.
fields.tab_content_3:
The signature waits for the insurance certificate

Initech Builders lets a drywall subcontractor sign only after insurance is on file. The agreement carries an upload slot for a certificate of insurance, and signing stays locked until one with a future expiry date is attached. The project manager gets an email to chase the renewal 30 days before that policy lapses.
fields.tab_content_4:
Questions that come before any contract

Globex asks the hiring manager six questions before a draft exists, such as who sets the hours. They follow the control tests the IRS uses to tell employees from contractors. When two or more answers point to employee-style control, the request goes to the HR lead and no agreement is generated.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Contractor Agreement
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write an independent contractor agreement that settles scope, pay, and ownership before the first invoice.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Fix the fee and the invoice terms
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Assign ownership of what gets made
fields.howto_step_1_des: Use the contractor's legal name, or the LLC or corporation they invoice through, with its state of formation. Signing with the person when the bank account belongs to the company makes the W-9 and every payment harder to match later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List what gets delivered by which date, with the number of revision rounds included. Leave out working hours and step-by-step methods. Instructions like those describe an employee, and they stay in the contract for anyone who reviews the relationship later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose a fixed fee or an hourly rate with a monthly cap, and state when invoices are due, such as net 15. Write down which expenses you reimburse and which the contractor carries, travel and software licenses especially.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Say who owns the finished work and when ownership moves, usually on final payment. Exclude anything the contractor brought with them, such as code libraries or design templates, and take a license to use those pieces inside your deliverable.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 State the relationship in plain terms
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write that the contractor runs their own business, sets their own schedule and receives no employee benefits. Treat this clause as a description, not a shield: if the daily work looks like employment, a sentence in the contract will not change that.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Agree on how either side can end it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set a notice period, such as 14 days in writing, and what happens at the end: payment for work completed so far and the handover of files and logins. Add a confidentiality clause that outlasts the contract.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sign it and keep it with the W-9
fields.howto_step_7_des: Collect both signatures before work starts, then store the agreement beside the contractor's W-9 and invoices. When a 1099-NEC is due or a scope dispute comes up, the signed copy is one search away from the payment history.

plan.angle: The top 10 is fill-in templates (LawDepot, Rocket Lawyer, eForms, SHRM) and one law-school sample that stop at a blank document. This page explains the clauses that decide disputes (scope, payment, IP assignment, termination, the classification language a contract cannot settle on its own), then builds what a template cannot: an intake form that drafts each agreement from the contractor's answers, collects the W-9 and signature, and tracks payments against the 1099-NEC threshold.
tab_stories: A brand studio hires a freelance illustrator, and the generated agreement adds a copyright assignment because a commissioned illustration is not automatically work made for hire; ownership passes on final payment.
An agency onboards 40 contractors a quarter: each fills the intake form, the app drafts the agreement and collects the W-9, and the ledger flags a contractor once 2026 payments reach $2,000.

A general contractor sends a drywall subcontractor the agreement, and the app holds it unsigned until a certificate of insurance with a future expiry date is uploaded, then reminds 30 days before the policy lapses.

Before any agreement is drafted, the hiring manager answers questions about schedule, tools and supervision, and answers that point to employee-style control send the request to the HR lead instead of generating a contract.

claims_to_source: A work created by an independent contractor is a work made for hire only if it falls in one of nine statutory categories and both parties sign a written agreement saying so
Businesses collect Form W-9 from contractors and file Form 1099-NEC for nonemployee compensation of $2,000 or more paid in 2026 ($600 before 2026)

The IRS uses common-law rules grouped as behavioral control, financial control and the type of relationship to decide whether a worker is an employee or an independent contractor; a contract label alone does not decide it
Under the federal ESIGN Act (15 U.S.C. 7001), a contract or signature may not be denied legal effect solely because it is in electronic form
Universities publish free sample independent contractor agreements

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Independent Contractor Agreement Generator'; hero 'Build an app that drafts an independent contractor agreement for each hire, collects the W-9, and files the signed copy.' covers drafting, tax paperwork and signing; howto_description one sentence.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is fill-in templates; the how-to walks the clauses (parties, deliverables, fee, IP, relationship, termination, signing), FAQ covers the template, free, 1099 and form questions, and the generator ships a drafted agreement per the sheet note.

specificity.evidence: Contractor-specific terms throughout: 'work made for hire', 'certificate of insurance', '1099-NEC', 'taxpayer ID'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs ('Drafts each agreement', 'Adds a copyright assignment'); tab paragraphs open on full sentences ('Northwind Agency signs on 40 contractors a quarter through a single intake.').

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; 'Treat this clause as a description, not a shield'.

voice.evidence: Operator detail: 'Signing with the person when the bank account belongs to the company makes the W-9 and every payment harder to match later.'

truth.evidence: Nine work-for-hire categories (circ30), $2,000 1099-NEC line for 2026 payments (i1099mec), IRS control tests (tc762) and ESIGN (15 USC 7001) match domain_sources; 2,400 + 2,400 = 4,800 and $2,350 over $2,000 agree in copy and images; claims map to claims_used incl. tax-records.

distinct.evidence: No HR sibling primary in headings; tabs are contractor-only stories (IP, W-9 ledger, COI lock, classification). Templated shapes shared with nda-form noted.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items, answer-first, hub link in item 2, sibling links (ACH form, creator application, employee information form), moat lines in items 5 and 8, no brands or formats in questions.
